title: 第11章 朝堂激辩，林大人威武
slug: 快活小御医恭喜皇后有喜了
content_zh:
第(1/3)页

“辩人心，抢占道德高地，给他们扣帽子！”

林墨背着手，开始一句一句地教。

“明天，那些老顽固，肯定会先声夺人，说我们与民争利。”

“你不要慌，等他们说完，第一句话就这么反问——”

林墨清了清嗓子，声情并茂道：

“请问各位大人，陛下这以工代赈之策，让食不果腹的灾民，靠自己的双手挣到饭吃，有活干，有钱拿，活得像个人，难道错了吗？’”

“还是说，在诸位达官贵人眼中，我大乾的子民，就只配跪在地上，像狗一样乞讨朝廷的残羹剩饭，才叫不与民争利？”

王喜听得目瞪口呆。

林墨继续道：“他们急眼后，肯定会跟你讲什么，不与民争利，这些古之圣贤道理。”

“你继续反问，圣贤是说过这话，可圣贤不是还说过——民为贵，社稷次之，君为轻吗？”

“如今江南百万灾民，流离失所，易子而食。”

“你们这些饱读诗书的君子，不想着如何让他们活下去，却在这里空谈什么与民争利！”

“你们的仁义之心呢？”

“你们对得起江南父老，对得起天下百姓吗？！”

林墨唾沫星子横飞，王喜在旁边听得是热血沸腾，仿佛自己已经成了那个舌战群儒的绝世辩才。

大半天时间，林墨没教他任何深奥的道理，只教了他三件事：如何偷换概念，如何抢占道德高地，以及如何用最朴素的民本思想，进行降维打击。

第二天，金銮殿上。

所有人都等着看王喜这个跳梁小丑，如何被以大儒张承言为首的民间士子，驳斥得体无完肤。

张承言果然如林墨所料，一上来就引经据典，洋洋洒洒，痛斥“以工代赈”是乱政、是恶法。

等他说完，所有人都看向瑟瑟发抖的王喜。

王喜深吸一口气，想起了昨晚林墨的教导，扯着嗓子就喊出了那句灵魂质问。

“请问张大人！”

“陛下让灾民有活干，有饭吃，有尊严，难道错了吗？！”

这一嗓子，直接把张承言给问懵了。

接下来，整个朝堂，就成了王喜一个人的表演舞台。

他完全按照林墨的剧本，时而悲愤填膺，时而声泪俱下。

将一场严肃的朝策辩论，硬生生扭转成了一场关于“真仁政”与“伪善”的道德审判大会。

他不说政策利弊，只说人命。

他不论民众得失，只论良心。

张承言等一众儒生，被他这套完全不按常理出牌的流氓打法，打得是节节败退，哑口无言。

他们空有一肚子经纶，却发现根本无处发力。

最后，当王喜指着他们的鼻子，向上天哭诉，喊出“难道你们的良心被狗吃了”的时候，胜负已分。

金銮殿上，一片死寂。

大儒张承言，这位在士林中德高望重，被无数读书人奉为楷模的老者，此刻一张脸已然涨成了猪肝色。

他伸出颤抖的手指，指着王喜，双眼激凸，嘴唇哆嗦着，喉咙里发出“嗬嗬”怪响。

“你……你……”

content_en:
Page (1/3)

"Advocate for people's hearts, seize the moral high ground, and slap them on their backs!"

Lin Mo put his hands behind his back and started teaching sentence by sentence.

"Tomorrow, those old stubborns will definitely take the lead and say that we are competing for profits with the people."

"Don't panic, wait until they finish speaking, and then ask this in the first sentence -"

Lin Mo cleared his throat and said with emotion:

"Excuse me, my lords, is it wrong for Your Majesty's work-for-relief policy to allow the hungry victims to earn food with their own hands, have work to do, have money to earn, and live like human beings?"

"Or, in the eyes of all the dignitaries, my people in Daqian are only worthy of kneeling on the ground and begging for leftovers from the court like dogs, so they don't compete with the people for profit?"

Wang Xi was stunned when he heard this.

Lin Mo continued: "When they are anxious, they will definitely tell you something, don't compete with the people for profit, these ancient sage principles."

"You continue to ask, the sages have said this, but didn't the sages also say that the people are the most valuable, the country is second, and the king is the least important?"

"Nowadays, millions of victims in the south of the Yangtze River have been displaced and exchanged their children for food."

"You gentlemen who have read poetry and books, don't think about how to let them live, but you are here talking about competing for profits with the people!"

"Where is your benevolence and righteousness?"

"Are you worthy of the elders of Jiangnan and the people of the world?!"

Lin Mo was spitting like flying stars, and Wang Xi's blood boiled with excitement as he listened, as if he had become the peerless eloquent speaker who could compete with other scholars.

For most of the day, Lin Mo didn't teach him any profound principles. He only taught him three things: how to secretly change concepts, how to seize the moral high ground, and how to use the simplest people-oriented thinking to carry out dimensionality reduction attacks.

The next day, at the Jinluan Hall.

Everyone was waiting to see how Wang Xi, a clown, would be completely refuted by the folk scholars headed by the great scholar Zhang Chengyan.

As expected by Lin Mo, Zhang Chengyan quoted scriptures and eloquently denounced "relief for work" as a disorder of government and a bad law.

After he finished speaking, everyone looked at the trembling Wang Xi.

Wang Xi took a deep breath, remembered Lin Mo's teaching last night, and shouted out the soul question at the top of his lungs.

"Excuse me, Master Zhang!"

"Your Majesty allows the victims to have work, food, and dignity. Is it wrong?"

This voice immediately confused Zhang Chengyan.

Next, the entire court became Wang Xi's performance stage alone.

He followed Lin Mo's script exactly, sometimes filled with grief and anger, sometimes bursting into tears.

A serious debate on government policy was abruptly turned into a moral trial conference about "true benevolent government" and "hypocrisy".

He doesn't talk about the pros and cons of policies, he only talks about human lives.

He doesn't care about the gains and losses of the people, he only cares about conscience.

Zhang Chengyan and other Confucian scholars were defeated and speechless by his rogue style of play, which was completely illogical.

They have a lot of money, but they find that they have nowhere to put their efforts.

Finally, when Wang Xi pointed at their noses, cried to heaven, and shouted, "Have your consciences been eaten by dogs?" the winner was decided.

There was deathly silence in the Jinluan Hall.

The great scholar Zhang Chengyan, this old man who was highly respected among scholars and was regarded as a role model by countless scholars, had a face that turned the color of pig liver at this moment.

He stretched out a trembling finger and pointed at Wang Xi. His eyes bulged, his lips trembled, and a strange "ho ho" sound came from his throat.

"You...you..."
